newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac, Kohl to confer after French election set.
newsitem.headline: Chirac, Kohl to confer after French election set.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac and German Chancellor Helmut Kohl will confer by telephone at 1830 GMT on Monday after Chirac dissolved parliament and called an early general election to prepare France for a single European currency, a presidential aide said.

The call symbolised the close consultation between the two driving forces behind European economic and monetary union, who have declared their intention to clear the decks domestically to ensure that the euro goes ahead on time in January 1999.
Kohl reaffirmed Germany's commitment to the single currency earlier this month by announcing -- also far ahead of schedule -- that he would run for re-election in late 1998.
Chirac applauded him publicly and the two conservative leaders met in Bonn on April 9 to coordinate their strategies.

In announcing his decision to call an election nine months before it was due, Chirac cited the need to be in a strong position for the next stages of European integration, including the "essential" switch to the euro.
